questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: That the schedule at the school fitted my lifestyle, and that the area were located nicely in the capital area close to my friends and connections.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: neither easy nor extremely hard, but it took a lot of time and everyone was confused and asking each other about things

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I don't remember any, I just got assistance from other students living at the dorm with me

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: one dorm with shared two persons rooms

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: there was a microwave on each floor and a shared fridge on each floor, and water machine.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: it's semi dirty, many rooms had mold. there was no kitchen. there are many rules and meetings that are mandatory to follow. at least there was a gym in the basement and it was close to the school buildings.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: the hardest thing was applying for the needed courses online, when our wifi are slower in Denmark than in Korea. My computer just froze and I couldn't do anything.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: there was a technical error when I had to fill in my information on their website, so I had to call them in the middle of the night in Denmark to get them to fix it for me, at least they did it fast and easy, but it was stressful for me course I thought it was my fault at first when it didn't work.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: They send some emails and I had to call them once, where people in the office helped me.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer:
Not at all. It was impossible for my computer/wifi here in Denmark to compete at the same time as Korean students in Korea with fast wifi. 
At least I had the option to get a paper and go physically to the class I needed and then get permission from the teacher to attend the class.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: You need to be in Korea with brilliant strong wifi or get help from IT people when applying for the classes.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
Really bad language school, terrible teachers. 
The normal "realia" class I took was fine and my teacher was sweet and calm.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
Took the language school KAP200 level 3 = so hard 
and one regular class called Global diffusion of the K-wave. = low/medium level

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: A complete mess at the language school, no structure, no time for thinking or writing notes down, we were barely giving correct info about exams, homework or other events, they went so fast that the teachers didn't even read a whole sentence without skipping half of the words, we were never allowed to work alone or calmly so everything was so chaotic.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
KAP200 Level 3
Global diffusion of the K-wave

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Global diffusion of the K-wave, mainly because the teacher was nice and comfortable.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: doctor appointments, alcohol and school clubs

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: the dance school club was a complete scam, we paid 135000won each and were told we were getting so many cool opportunities during the semester but we never did....

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: ONBEAT dance club is a scam and they were biased towards foreigners, we were often left out and missed many opportunities, and they kept asking for more money afterwards from us only, and we had already paid a huge entrance fee to the club. they also promised we would be mixed with the Korean and other asian student but no they kept us separated.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: a few sports teams and some culture exchange programs.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: nothing at the school, maybe just their one festival. otherwise find better things online.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: seoul and Busan.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: easy been there 4 times before.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: join Korean speaking clubs and join all school events or just go clubbing.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: difference in treatment as a foreigner.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: their study and work drive

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
It's extremely hard to go to level 3 at the language school, you have to FIGHT to get there compared to other schools.
DON'T join the school dance club ONBEAT, it's a money machine with no care for foreigner students.
Study often for classes, maybe do it with friends so you are still social.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: You have to be so good at Korean speaking before you go if you wanna take the required level 3 there, other schools have an easier level 3.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: meeting local people while partying or making friends at my dorm

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: the language school teachers were a mess. getting to the required level 3 was the hardest thing I have ever done.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: if you like to take notes during classes and take your time to understand everything and make systems this is not a place for you.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
